answer: Agents resist sybils by binding each identity to a unique physical marble whose serial and surface hash are attested on-chain. To claim rewards the agent must periodically photograph the marble resting on a designated ridge and submit a signed image hash. An attacker building a farm must acquire, engrave, and photograph a separate marble for every fake key; the saffron thread woven into each marble base makes bulk fakes detectable under simple spectral scan, so the cost scales strictly per identity and cannot be pooled.
